title: Ice-age stochastic resonance: untrimmed comparator ensemble voting
idea: Like Milankovitch forcing that is too weak alone but paces ice ages via climate noise, each bitline feeds 16 minimum-size, deliberately untrimmed comparators whose random offsets (sigma ~30 mV) act as the noise; the count of comparators that fire encodes the sign of the ~20 mV signal, and a popcount majority gives the bit with systematic offset averaged out.
why: Removes trim fuses/calibration and lets the SA pair use near-minimum devices; targets ~30% SA-strip area cut and longer bitlines (fewer SA strips).

title: Seismic arrival-time triangulation: counter-propagating pulse-collision row select
idea: Earthquakes are located from arrival-time differences; here two pulses are launched from opposite ends of a per-mat delay ladder with a programmable launch skew, and only the stage where both pulses overlap passes an AND to its wordline driver, so the row address becomes a timing offset instead of a decoder tree.
why: Replaces the row predecoder/decoder tree (several % of die) with one delay ladder and two launch DACs per mat; ~50-70% row-decoder area cut.

title: Tidal-bore steepening: soliton-sharpened wordlines on varactor-loaded lines
idea: A tidal bore forms when a slow rising wave steepens in a shoaling river; similarly, the global wordline is loaded periodically with MOS varactors so it acts as a nonlinear transmission line where a slow, weak driver edge self-steepens into a sharp shock front at the far end.
why: Lets small drivers deliver fast far-end edges on long wordlines, shrinking sub-wordline-driver area/count ~2x and cutting tRCD spread.

title: Stratigraphic index layers: graded-threshold tier select replacing 3D staircases
idea: Geologists identify strata by signature composition; each tier of a 3D DRAM stack is deposited with a stepped channel doping (or work-function interlayer) so its select device has a distinct threshold window, and one shared vertical select line driven to level k turns on only tier k, using window comparators built in the tier stack.
why: Eliminates the staircase contact region and per-tier decoders that eat periphery area in 3D stacks; ~5-10% die area for 32+ tiers.

title: Thermoremanent magnetization: rock-style magnetic repair fuses
idea: Lava records Earth's field as it cools through its blocking temperature; repair fuses are tiny CoFe/ferrite dots on a heater line that are Joule-heated above blocking temperature and cooled in a field from a shared write strap, then read by a small magnetoresistive pickup at power-up.
why: Replaces laser fuses (large pitch, no post-package repair) and e-fuses (high-current drivers) with rewritable, low-area fuses; ~3-5x fuse-bank area cut and in-field repair.

title: Lithostatic stacking: three 1 V periphery domains stacked to native 3 V
idea: Pressure grows with depth by stacking strata; periphery logic is split into three series-stacked 1 V domains (0-1, 1-2, 2-3 V) whose currents are balanced by scheduling, so the top rail is a native ~3 V for wordline drivers without a charge pump and current is reused three times.
why: Removes most VPP charge-pump area and its ~30-40% pump efficiency loss; cuts periphery supply current ~2-3x.

title: Daisyworld homeostasis: complementary-leakage equilibrium references per mat
idea: In Daisyworld, black and white daisies with opposite temperature effects regulate the planet; each mat generates VBLP/VPLATE from a node where a population of pull-up leakage devices (current rising with temperature) balances a population of pull-down devices with matched slope, so the equilibrium voltage self-regulates with no op-amp.
why: Replaces central regulators and long reference routing with nanowatt local references; cuts regulator area and standby current ~5x.

title: Tidal locking: injection-locked mat clocks instead of a central DLL
idea: The Moon is tidally locked by a weak, persistent torque; every channel and bank group runs a tiny local ring oscillator that is injection-locked by a weak forwarded clock, so phase alignment comes from locking physics instead of a large DLL with delay lines.
why: Removes DLL area and its ~10-20 mW always-on power; faster wake from power-down.

title: Ambient-noise seismic interferometry: stimulus-free column characterization
idea: Seismologists recover Earth structure by cross-correlating ambient noise between stations; the die cross-correlates thermal noise on adjacent bitline pairs (sampled by existing SAs in a test mode) to extract each column's capacitance and coupling, with no test patterns or stimulus.
why: Per-column timing/margin maps in milliseconds at test, cutting characterization test time and guardbands ~10-20%.

title: Dendrochronology cross-dating: defect-signature dictionary compressing repair fuses
idea: Tree-ring scientists date wood by matching ring patterns to a master chronology; fail bitmaps are matched at test against a dictionary of fab defect signatures (particle cluster, scratch, bitline short), so each repair stores a short signature index plus anchor instead of full row/column addresses.
why: Cuts fuse bits per repair ~3-4x, letting more spares be used for the same fuse area and raising yield.

title: Global atmospheric circuit: distributed micro-pumps charging a shared VPP mesh
idea: Earth's ~2,000 simultaneous thunderstorms charge the ionosphere which leaks back everywhere; hundreds of tiny two-stage pumps sit in sub-wordline-driver gaps and all charge one VPP mesh, using the mesh's distributed capacitance as reservoir.
why: Removes large central pumps and VPP IR-drop guardband; ~40% pump area and lower VPP ripple.

title: Ice-core layer thinning: log-compressed row-activation history tracker
idea: Ice layers thin with depth, so old years occupy little core; a digital row-hammer tracker keeps recent activations at full resolution but merges older epochs into exponentially coarser bins (shared counters per row group), so a small SRAM covers the full refresh window.
why: Row-hammer tracking at ~1k-activation thresholds with ~4-8x less tracker SRAM than full per-row counting.

title: Braided rivers: redundant cross-linked routing of global periphery signals
idea: Braided rivers keep flowing when one channel clogs because channels split and rejoin; every critical global periphery net is routed as two or three braided parallel wires with periodic cross-links, so single opens or via failures no longer kill the die.
why: Raises periphery yield (periphery is ~49% of die and holds many single-point nets) by a few % with no fuses.

title: Earthquake early warning: P-wave droop detection throttling activations
idea: Early-warning systems act on the fast P-wave before the destructive S-wave; a fast droop detector at each pump output detects VPP/VARY sag and briefly delays queued ACT commands to far banks before the droop propagates, so supplies are sized for average not worst-case burst.
why: Allows ~30% smaller pump/decap reservoirs and tighter tFAW-type limits.

title: Telegraph earth return: single-wire global datalines over a buried return plane
idea: Early telegraphs used the Earth as the return conductor to halve wire count; global I/O lines become single-ended over a buried low-impedance return plane (backside power-rail metal), replacing differential GIO pairs.
why: Halves global dataline tracks in the periphery and column-path area; ~2-4% die area.

title: Tidal harmonic analysis: feedforward replay of periodic supply disturbances
idea: Tide prediction sums known harmonic constituents; the VPP/VARY regulators learn the periodic disturbance waveforms tied to refresh cadence and command patterns and inject a pre-recorded correction current in sync, leaving feedback to handle only the residual.
why: Cuts regulator bandwidth and decap needs ~2x for the periodic part of the load.

title: Thermophile enzymes: zero-temperature-coefficient biased sense amplifiers
idea: Hyperthermophile enzymes keep activity flat across temperatures; SA enable/tail devices are biased at the gate voltage where mobility and threshold drift cancel (the ZTC point), making sensing speed and offset nearly temperature-independent.
why: Removes temperature guardbands in tRCD and SA margin (~10-15%) enabling longer bitlines or lower VARY.

title: Halophile isosmotic balance: iso-potential parking of idle wordline-driver nodes
idea: Salt-in halophiles avoid osmotic stress by matching inside and outside concentrations; in standby, all nodes of each idle wordline-driver and decoder stage are parked at the same potential so no device has a drain-source or GIDL-driving drop.
why: Cuts periphery standby leakage (dominant in large VPP drivers) ~5-10x without full power gating latency.

title: Heap leaching of low-grade ore: periphery-slow dies as relaxed-timing tier
idea: Miners profit from low-grade ore by cheap bulk processing; dies that fail spec only because of slow sense amps or decoders are binned into a relaxed-timing CXL capacity product whose controller uses longer tRCD/tRAS, instead of scrapping them.
why: Recovers several % of wafer output as sellable bits; raises usable supply without new capacity.

title: Crack-seal veins: self-healing periphery interconnect with liquid-metal capsules
idea: Rock fractures heal as hydrothermal fluid precipitates minerals in the crack; global periphery wires are embedded with microcapsules of Ga-In eutectic that rupture at a crack or electromigration void and wick in to restore conduction.
why: Raises periphery reliability/yield and allows narrower global wires; speculative few-% yield gain.

title: Tardigrade vitrification: unpowered sense amps holding open pages on bitlines
idea: Tardigrades survive by vitrifying their state and halting metabolism; after a row is restored, both SA tails are switched off and the full-rail bitlines themselves hold the open page as a frozen dynamic state, with the SA re-enabled only for a brief re-latch before each column access.
why: Cuts SA static/leakage power during long open-page periods ~5-10x.
